title: Obituary, eulogy, memorial tribute, and the public grammar of a life

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source afterward/bereavement/funeral-language synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no individual legal, financial, funeral, clinical, mental-health, or ritual advice.
limitations: Public sources support broad vocabulary and practical context only; they do not supply consented room texture.
This record must not become legal, estate, financial, funeral, clinical, mental-health, diagnosis, ritual, or crisis advice.
Local law, institutional policy, funeral-home/cemetery/crematory requirements, clinicians, mental-health professionals, guardians, tradition holders, and the person’s wishes govern actual decisions.

moment.plain_scene: The bereaved or community must turn a life into public words: obituary, death notice, eulogy, tribute, order of service, memorial page, or “celebration of life.”
ordinary_language_queries: how to write obituary after death
what do you say in a memorial tribute

content_layers.observation_text: The bereaved or community must turn a life into public words: obituary, death notice, eulogy, tribute, order of service, memorial page, or “celebration of life.”
content_layers.source_synthesis: Public funeral sources mention funeral-related announcements and services; grief sources support that culture, relationship, and circumstances shape grief expression. This record has high literary/social-language value but needs source expansion into obituaries and memorial archives.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: The obituary is a compression engine: it selects kinship, work, virtues, euphemism, cause-of-death silence, “fighter” tropes, and who counts as family. It belongs in DeathVocab because public language is part of dying’s aftermath.

what_this_is_not: not a rule about cause-of-death disclosure
not permission to mine identifiable memorial pages without consent or careful public-source policy
uncertainties: Obituary and memorial language is culturally, regionally, religiously, class, age, and platform specific.
Cause-of-death disclosure may implicate privacy, stigma, suicide-safe messaging, and living-family consent.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should make the phrase findable, orient the reader to why the moment is common enough to name, and then stop before giving personal legal, financial, funeral, mental-health, clinical, or ritual advice.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner or researcher surface should collect who had authority, what words were used, what the setting required, what the family understood, where conflict or exclusion appeared, and which local/professional supports were involved.
language_notes: Do not treat grief as a stage, task, timetable, performance, or disorder unless a qualified diagnostic context exists.
Keep legal, funeral, financial, child, and ritual content jurisdiction- and authority-bound.
Preserve ordinary words the bereaved use, including euphemism, anger, numbness, absence, and administrative speech.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the afterward, funeral/disposition, administrative-burden, and grief-language layer. It requires domain review before any public surface uses it.

safety.cultural_sensitivity: medium_to_high_because funeral body grief and family authority are culture bound
safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a diagnosis, not therapy, not crisis support, not legal advice, not estate or financial advice, not funeral consumer advice, not a ritual authority, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for local clinicians, hospice, emergency services, mental-health or crisis support, funeral directors, registrars, coroners/medical examiners, legal/financial professionals, guardians, tradition holders, or local law.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through bereavement, tone, jurisdiction/legal, child-safety where applicable, funeral/disposition, accessibility, cultural, and source-card review. Any surface must route urgent, unsafe, contested, legal, money, funeral, child, or mental-health situations to qualified local support.
